conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and cutting positions below stops. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Reduce leveraged ETF exposure in SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and PLTU.
Sell SMH and SMCI as they are below their stops.
Blend broad index and quality tech with small leverage.
Maintain a cash buffer of approximately 10%.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining some exposure to growth assets. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Increase exposure to SOXL and MUU, leveraging strong scanner setups.
Sell SMH and SMCI as they are below their stops, reallocating capital.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It uses and adds leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of significantly higher drawdown potential and daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to zero.

income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index for steady distributions. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in selloffs; this is not a savings account.
